questions.q: What table does a UI Policy record live on?
options: sys_ui_policy
sys_data_policy2
sys_script
sc_cat_item
questions.explain: A UI Policy is a record on sys_ui_policy, scoped to one table, with a condition and related UI Policy Actions.

questions.q: A UI Policy Action can apply which three effects to a field?
options: Encrypt, archive, and audit the field
Visible, mandatory, and read-only
Rename, resize, and reorder the field
Export, import, and index the field
questions.explain: Those are the only three field-level effects a UI Policy Action controls: show/hide, require, or lock from editing.

questions.q: What does "reverse if false" do on a UI Policy Action?
options: It deletes the UI Policy Action once the condition is false
It sends an email notification to the admin
It automatically undoes the action's effect once its condition is no longer true
It converts the UI Policy into a Data Policy
questions.explain: With reverse if false on, the field's behavior snaps back the moment the triggering condition stops being true — e.g. the field re-hides itself.

questions.q: Why does a UI Policy evaluate instantly as a user changes a field, with no page reload?
options: It runs entirely client-side, in the browser, re-checking its condition live as the form changes
It silently reloads the page in the background every time
It runs on the ServiceNow server after every keystroke
It only evaluates once, when the form first opens
questions.explain: UI Policies are a client-side mechanism — the condition and field effects are evaluated in the browser as the user interacts with the form.

questions.q: An integration creates a Hardware-category Incident via a Scripted REST API, leaving Asset Tag blank, even though a UI Policy makes Asset Tag mandatory when Category is Hardware. What happens?
options: The API call is rejected because the UI Policy blocks it
The record saves with Asset Tag blank, because the UI Policy never evaluates outside the browser form
ServiceNow automatically fills in a default Asset Tag value
The Incident is created but immediately deleted by the platform
questions.explain: UI Policies only govern the rendered form in the browser. A REST API write never touches the form, so the mandatory rule is never enforced — this is the exact gap Data Policies exist to close.
